structure: Layout of script placement records (ScriptSet "set [set]||to" wrappers) and the header-table entry they embed

location.offset: 30 positioned instances in the tutorial file, e.g. 0x34959C/0x34AC18 (0x1C8), 0x34AA34 (0x1E4), 0x34D850/0x232258/0x2B7BF0 (0x198), 0x1E0490 (0x140); embedded type-104 entries at +0x48: 0x3495E4, 0x34AC60, 0x34AA7C, 0x34D898, 0x2322A0, 0x2B7C38

meaning: Every placement the header table lists is a type-104 record at +0x48 of a type-111 wrapper carrying the same name; the wrapper holds the transform and, depending on its size class, the model (inline path or type-64 reference), companions and an optional behaviour script. Same-size replacement therefore overwrites a table-listed record in place with another of the same type: the table, the count-bounded walks and the relocation stay consistent, which is why --replace-record works with zero shift. Pointer offsets come from the runtime fixup map (words rewritten in RAM), not from heuristics; the size classes and their extra fields were read on all 30 instances.
